sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant; and learned A.G.A. for the State/opposite party no. 1.
2.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant to quash the charge sheet dated 22.02.2023; cognizance order dated 02.09.2023 as well as entire criminal proceedings of Crl. Case No.5390 of 2023 (State Vs. Amir Kirmani) relating to Case Crime No. 236 of 2022,
under sections 420, 406, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Biharigarh, District Saharanpur.
3.

Brief facts of the case are that informant met with applicant in Dehradun, Uttarakhan where applicant told to the opposite party no. 2, that he has some land at Ganeshpur bearing Khasra No. 4,
Amir Kirmani vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155180356/
1 admeasuring 2 bigha.

entities.text: Amir Kirmani vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On believing the applicant, opposite party no. 2 agreed to purchase the land at the rate of Rs. ten lac per bigha, bearing Khasra No. 4 area 2 bigha.

The opposite party no. 2 gave Rs.
5 lac cash and ten lac through R.T.G.S.
The opposite party no. 2 contacted the applicant to execute sale deed but the applicant procrastinated and did not execute the sale deed.
Opposite party no. 2 got information that the applicant is not owner of the plot and has no concern with the said land.
Then, the opposite party no. 2 contacted applicant for returning money but the applicant did not return the money and also threatened him of dire consequences.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that no offence under the aforesaid sections is made out.
He next submits that entire proceeding is barred by territorial jurisdiction as informant met with applicant in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, offence cannot be proceeded in instant jurisdiction.
The proceedings is illegal and abuse of the process of the law.

In support of his submission, counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon the judgement of Apex Court in Premkumar and others Vs. State of Kerala over paragraphs No. 8, 9, 13, 14, and 17.
5.

entities.text: Premkumar and others Vs. State of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer of the applicant and submits that instant proceeding cannot be entertained in territorial jurisdiction as offence has been committed in Dehradun, Uttarakhand.

6. On perusal of F.I.R., allegation is that applicant and informant met in Dehradun, Uttarakhand and applicant showed paper of land situated in Saharanpur district,U.P. claiming themself owner of land and proposed to sell to informant.
The informant was ready to purchase the land of applicant and in pursuance thereof, informant paid Rs.50 lac through cash and Rs.10 lac through RTGS.
Thereafter, the informant got information that land does not belong to applicant wherein the informant asked for returning of the said amount.
The applicant refused to return the same.

The submission made by counsel for the applicant that as money was paid in Dehradun, the instant F.I.R. cannot be lodged in Saharanpur, U.P.
7.
In view of the provision provided under Sections 177, 178 and 179 Cr.P.C. wherein code provide jurisdiction of the criminal courts in inquiries and trials.
Section 177 Cr.P.C. provides that every offence shall ordinarily be inquired into and tried by a Court within whose local jurisdiction it was committed.

Applicant duped the informant by declaring himself as owner of the property which is situated in District Saharanpur and the court of District Saharanpur has territorial jurisdiction and has entertained the police report.
Argument of the counsel for the applicant that no incident occurred in territorial jurisdiction of district Saharanpur having no force and is rejected.
The reliance placed by the counsel for the applicant is not applicable in the present case.
8. In view of the above, the order passed by the trial court is just and proper and no interference is warranted, at this stage.
9. The present 482 application is hereby dismissed.
